EXP255-E01 · Matched-pair media-publication experiment 01 (pair identity not reported)

Class 1 · One of the 35 distinct matched-pair randomized experiments reported in the main article. Each used a different pack/subject/time manipulation and contributes two week observations to pooled n=70 inference. The article does not identify or report this pair separately, so its experiment-specific content and result are NR; numbering is an inventory device, not an inferred chronology.

Experiment design: cluster-randomized experiment

Design map

Target population

Americans participating in public social-media discussion in 11 broad policy areas, exposed to publication by participating mostly small news outlets; a formal target-population definition is NR.
among those able to participate in social mediaPDF page 5 · Fig. 3 discussion

The subgroup conclusion is explicitly bounded to people able to participate in social media.

a set of 11 areasPDF page 3 · Treatment protocol, lower right column

The article lists the 11 eligible policy areas, from race and immigration through reproductive rights.

Eligibility criteria

Partial: outlets needed relevant experience and enthusiasm and volunteered for each pack; complete outlet, article, user, and post eligibility criteria are NR.
allowed outlets to volunteer to join a packPDF page 4 · Treatment protocol, lower left column

Outlets volunteered for a pack after the researchers sought experience in and enthusiasm for the policy area, but no complete eligibility rule is given.

Recruitment procedure

48 mostly small outlets were enlisted over nearly five years, with help from The Media Consortium; the contact/sampling procedure and refusals are NR.
Forty-eight mostly small news media outlets participatedPDF page 3 · Methods narrative, left column

Forty-eight outlets participated overall; 17 were involved in preliminary trials and 33 in the reported protocol, with two overlapping.

Field dates and setting

October 2014–March 2016; United States nation-week interventions involving outlet publication and public social-media posts.
between October 2014 and March 2016PDF page 5 · Results narrative, lower left column

The intervention ran from October 2014 through March 2016 in the United States and concerned national social-media discussion.

Number recruited and analyzed

For this individual matched pair: exact outlets recruited/participating are NR (only the 2–5 range is given); two randomized week observations are implied and included in the pooled n=70 analysis. Counts of posts/authors analyzed are NR.
Forty-eight mostly small news media outlets participatedPDF page 3 · Methods narrative, left column

Forty-eight outlets participated overall; 17 were involved in preliminary trials and 33 in the reported protocol, with two overlapping.

35 experiments and thus n = 70 observationsPDF page 5 · Results narrative, lower left column

Sequential stopping produced 35 matched week-pairs, analyzed as 70 week observations.

Experimental arms or randomized attributes

Two arms within each week-pair: pack publication week and business-as-usual control week.
randomly assigned one week to be the ‘treatment’ weekPDF page 4 · Randomization description, upper right column

Within each matched pair of consecutive weeks, exactly one week was assigned treatment and the other control.

asked to behave as usualPDF page 4 · Randomization description, upper right column

Treatment was pack publication on the chosen day (usually Tuesday); during the control week outlets behaved as usual.

Unit of randomization

The entire nation during an experiment-week, randomized within a matched pair of consecutive weeks.
unit of treatment was the entire nation during an experiment-weekPDF page 4 · Randomization description, upper right column

The randomization/treatment unit was the nation during an experiment-week.

randomly assigned one week to be the ‘treatment’ weekPDF page 4 · Randomization description, upper right column

Within each matched pair of consecutive weeks, exactly one week was assigned treatment and the other control.

Allocation probabilities and restrictions

Exactly one of two consecutive matched weeks was treatment and one control (implying two allowed allocations and equal assignment under the named matched-pair randomization); weeks were selected for predicted-news similarity. Further restrictions are NR.
randomly assigned one week to be the ‘treatment’ weekPDF page 4 · Randomization description, upper right column

Within each matched pair of consecutive weeks, exactly one week was assigned treatment and the other control.

Exact treatment and comparator

Treatment: 2–5 outlets publish one article each on their chosen subject within a researcher-chosen policy area, usually Tuesday, and distribute/promote normally. Comparator: behave as usual. Exact outlets, subjects, and articles are intentionally not disclosed.
a ‘pack’ of two to five outletsPDF page 4 · Treatment protocol, lower columns

Each intervention used two to five outlets (mean 3.1), with a pack selecting a subject inside the researcher-chosen policy area.

asked to behave as usualPDF page 4 · Randomization description, upper right column

Treatment was pack publication on the chosen day (usually Tuesday); during the control week outlets behaved as usual.

Outcome definitions and timing

Daily days 1–6 and total-week counts/percent changes of posts in the broad policy area; daily/weekly unique-author counts; subgroup and ideological-composition outcomes are mentioned. Rules classifying posts, authors, ideology, and policy areas are NR.
total number of posts in a broad policy areaPDF page 5 · Figs. 2 and 4; results narrative

The main outcome is the daily and weekly total count of posts in the intervention's broad policy area; Fig. 4 uses daily unique authors.

increase of 23.9% in the number of unique authorsPDF page 5 · Fig. 4 discussion

The first-day unique-author effect is 23.9%, or 3,287 additional authors.

Estimand

Average causal effect of pack publication at a randomized time on public expression in the chosen broad policy area, reported daily and over the week.
average causal effect of a pack of journalists publishing articlesPDF page 5 · Paragraph introducing Fig. 2

Effect estimates and uncertainty

Effects include 19.4%/4,442 posts on day 1, 62.7%/13,166 posts over the week, and 23.9%/3,287 authors on day 1. Numerical SEs/CIs are NR.
